observations:
Torah #211 is a three-sentence teaching with only 2 bechina edges in the dataset, yielding 4 nodes distributed across 2 packages. The two proposed packages (Package 1: מֹחִין וּמֹשֶׁה; Package 2: צַדִּיק וְיוֹסֵף) exhaust the bechina conceptual space of the Torah.

No independent bechina domain of 3+ concepts was found in the source text that is structurally separate from the existing two packages.

The following candidate domains were examined and rejected as new packages:

1. הַמְתָּקַת הַדִּינִין (sweetening of judgments) — This is the goal/outcome of the teaching, not an independent bechina cluster. It appears only in an eitza edge (edge 884: purity of thought → sweetening of judgments). The teaching does not equate it to anything else via 'בְּחִינַת' language; it is the stated purpose, not a conceptual peer. No bechina family of 3+ nodes can be assembled around it.

2. רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (Rosh Hashana) — Rosh Hashana is the occasion/context of the teaching, not developed into a bechina cluster. The statement 'רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הוּא מְקוֹר הַדִּינִים' uses 'הוּא' (is) rather than 'בְּחִינַת' and is a factual description of the day's spiritual function, not a bechina declaration that would seed a new package. No further bechina equivalences are drawn from it in the text.

3. הִתְקַשְּׁרוּת לְצַדִּיקִים (attachment to tzaddikim) — This concept appears in two eitza edges as the cause that produces pure intellect. It was examined as a bechina candidate for Package 2 (see additions file). Even if accepted as a bechina node attached to Package 2 (tzaddik/Yosef domain), it does not constitute a new independent package — it is an extension of Package 2, not a new thematic family.

4. Evil mirror — No evil package is warranted for Torah #211. The teaching contains no evil personifications, no evil domain names, no opposing force described with bechina equivalences. The judgments (דינים) of Rosh Hashana are a neutral structural element of the teaching (they must be sweetened), but they are not developed into an evil cluster. This Torah is entirely prescriptive and positive in its conceptual development.

Conclusion: The two packages proposed in torah_211_packages.json fully account for all bechina-connected nodes in the dataset. The Torah's extreme brevity means that what would in a longer Torah become multiple packages here reduces to the minimal dyad: the mochin/intellect domain and the tzaddik/righteous-one domain. The teaching's argument is their mutual dependency — mochin needs tzaddik for its completion — expressed through the Moshe-Yosef model.
